# Fork releases

CI1 and CI2 dispatch `fork-desktop-release.yml` on the fork default branch after a complete sync, with `sync_sha` and `upstream_sha` set to the full fork and upstream commit IDs. An up-to-date sync sends the same pair. Paused and partial runs do not dispatch nightlies. Hourly reconciliation also discovers published upstream GitHub Releases with `dsh-v<version>` tags, including RCs. Starting at CI3 installation, CI3 builds the first fork checkpoint whose integrated upstream master contains the peeled release tag and whose fork and master product versions both match. The release manifest records the fork head in `commit`, the master parent in `upstreamCommit`, and the peeled tag SHA in `upstreamTagCommit`.

Each `fork-v<version>` or `fork-nightly-<full fork SHA>` release contains unsigned Linux x64, Windows x64, and Apple Silicon desktop installers and CLI archives. Extract the CLI archive and run `dsh` or `dsh.cmd`. The archive includes Node and pnpm. `SHA256SUMS` and `fork-release.json` identify the bytes, source commits and package version. macOS uses a local ad-hoc signature and manual DMG installation.

The `fork-feed` release in `LianZiZhou/deepseek-harness` hosts updater metadata under `releases/download/fork-feed/`. Windows uses `stable.yml` or `nightly.yml`, Linux uses `stable-linux.yml` or `nightly-linux.yml`, and the CLI can read `stable.json` or `nightly.json`. The stable feed follows the highest official product version, including upstream prereleases. The nightly feed follows the newest built full-sync head in fork first-parent order. Each feed file points directly to an immutable fork release. Only completed sets become public. Re-running reconciliation repairs interrupted uploads. GitHub replaces each public feed asset individually. If replacement is interrupted, that channel can be temporarily unavailable until reconciliation repairs it.
